b1-democratizacion-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Back to the Ballot Box
b1-democratizacion-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos watched a documentary about the end of the dictatorships, and he asks which countries came back to elected government first.
b1-democratizacion-01.prompt: Tell Carlos which countries returned first and which one came at the end.
cues: Say which two countries returned first and in which years
Say which country came at the end, using an ordering marker
b1-democratizacion-01.target: Primero volvieron Ecuador, en 1979, y Perú, en 1980. Finalmente, en 1990, Chile tuvo otra vez un presidente civil.
b1-democratizacion-01.english: First Ecuador returned, in 1979, and Peru, in 1980. Finally, in 1990, Chile had a civilian president again.
b1-democratizacion-01.canDo: I can list the countries that returned to elected government and the years.

b1-democratizacion-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The New Constitutions
b1-democratizacion-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg visited a museum exhibition about the 1980s, and she asks what the new constitution of Brazil did.
b1-democratizacion-02.prompt: Tell Meg what Brazil's constitution of 1988 recognised and what was created.
cues: Say when the Congress enacted the constitution and what it recognised
Say what was created, without saying who created it
b1-democratizacion-02.target: En Brasil, el Congreso promulgó una nueva constitución en 1988, y reconoció muchos derechos sociales. Se creó un servicio de salud pública para todos.
b1-democratizacion-02.english: In Brazil, the Congress enacted a new constitution in 1988, and it recognised many social rights. A public health service for everyone was created.
b1-democratizacion-02.canDo: I can say what Brazil's constitution of 1988 recognised.

b1-democratizacion-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Rights and Courts
b1-democratizacion-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are telling Carlos what you read in a book about justice in the new democracies, and he asks whether people could use their rights.
b1-democratizacion-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what the problem was and what the tutela allowed.
cues: Admit a difficulty and go on
Say what a person could ask a judge to do with the tutela
b1-democratizacion-03.target: A pesar de que la ley reconocía los derechos, mucha gente pobre no podía defenderlos. Con la tutela, una persona podía pedir a un juez la protección de un derecho.
b1-democratizacion-03.english: Although the law recognised rights, many poor people could not defend them. With the tutela, a person could ask a judge to protect a right.
b1-democratizacion-03.canDo: I can say why justice was still a problem after the dictatorships.

b1-democratizacion-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Presidents in Trouble
b1-democratizacion-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are going over a class on the 1990s, and she asks what power the military kept in Chile after the dictatorship.
b1-democratizacion-04.prompt: Tell Meg what stopped in Chile and what the military kept.
cues: Say what the military stopped doing
b1-democratizacion-04.target: Los militares dejaron de gobernar en Chile, pero Pinochet siguió como comandante en jefe del Ejército hasta 1998.
b1-democratizacion-04.english: The military stopped governing in Chile, but Pinochet remained commander in chief of the army until 1998.
b1-democratizacion-04.canDo: I can say what power the military kept in Chile after 1990.

b1-democratizacion-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Imperfect Democracies
b1-democratizacion-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are talking about a book on the new democracies, and he asks what the author concludes.
b1-democratizacion-05.prompt: Sum up what the region had and what it still needed to do.
cues: Begin with a summing-up marker and say what the region had
Say what the countries still had to do
b1-democratizacion-05.target: En resumen, la región tenía democracias, pero muchas eran imperfectas. Todavía tenían problemas: la corrupción y la desigualdad.
b1-democratizacion-05.english: In summary, the region had democracies, but many were imperfect. They still had problems: corruption and inequality.
b1-democratizacion-05.canDo: I can sum up what the new democracies had and what problems they still had.

b1-democratizacion-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The New Democracies in Order
b1-democratizacion-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are going over your notes before a class, and she asks you to tell how the countries returned to elections and what problems came after.
b1-democratizacion-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg in order how the countries returned to elections and what problems came after.
cues: Say what the military kept in Chile
Sum up with a closing marker
b1-democratizacion-consolidation.target: Primero volvieron Ecuador y Perú. Después, los militares dejaron de gobernar, pero en Chile conservaron poder. En resumen, había democracias, pero tenían problemas.
b1-democratizacion-consolidation.english: First Ecuador and Peru returned. Then the military stopped governing, but in Chile they kept power. In summary, there were democracies, but they had problems.
b1-democratizacion-consolidation.canDo: I can retell in order how the countries of Latin America returned to elected government.
